regimes.name: SOC 2 (2017 TSC, 2022 Points of Focus)
regimes.applies_when: customers or partners ask for assurance over the service's security posture; B2B SaaS almost always
regimes.challenge: unanswered -- select applicable or not (`wall compliance soc2 ...`)

controls.statement: Control environment: integrity, oversight, accountability are real and assigned
Communication and information: policies reach the people they bind
Risk assessment: risks identified, analyzed, and responded to on a cadence
Monitoring: controls are evaluated and deficiencies reach the right people
Control activities: controls exist at the process level, not just on paper
Logical and physical access: least privilege, credential lifecycle, boundary protection
System operations: anomaly detection, incident response, recovery
Change management: changes authorized, tested, approved, tracked
Risk mitigation: vendor and business-disruption risk handled
Availability (optional category): capacity, backup, recovery objectives met
Processing integrity (optional): processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely
Confidentiality (optional): confidential data identified and protected to disposal
Privacy (optional): personal information handled per the privacy notice

regimes.name: Healthcare privacy (HIPAA/PHI, Part 2, HBNR, info blocking)
regimes.applies_when: the system creates, receives, maintains or transmits protected health information, or serves one that does (business associate)
regimes.challenge: unanswered -- select applicable or not (`wall compliance hipaa ...`)

controls.statement: Administrative safeguards (164.308): risk analysis, workforce training, access management, contingency plan
Physical safeguards (164.310): facility access, workstation and device controls
Technical safeguards (164.312): access control, audit controls, integrity, transmission security, encryption
Organizational (164.314): BAAs with every business associate -- a hosted LLM included
Policies and documentation (164.316): written, retained six years, updated
Privacy Rule: minimum necessary uses and disclosures
Breach Notification (164.400s): discovery clocks, individual and HHS notice
42 CFR Part 2 (in force 2026-02-16, OCR-enforced): SUD records identified, segregated, consent-tracked; NPP updated
FTC Health Breach Notification Rule (2024): non-HIPAA health data in apps/devices covered, breach clocks known
Information blocking + certified health IT (ASTP/ONC): no practice that blocks EHI; certification duties current where the product is certified

regimes.name: PCI DSS v4.0.1
regimes.applies_when: cardholder data is stored, processed or transmitted, or the system can affect the security of a payment flow
regimes.challenge: unanswered -- select applicable or not (`wall compliance pci ...`)

controls.statement: Network security controls installed and maintained
Secure configurations applied to all system components
Stored account data protected (no PAN in logs or fixtures, ever)
Cardholder data encrypted over open, public networks
Malicious software protected against
Secure systems and software developed and maintained
Access restricted by business need to know
Users identified and access authenticated (MFA)
Physical access to cardholder data restricted
Access to system components and cardholder data logged and monitored
Security of systems and networks tested regularly
Information security supported by organizational policies (incl. 12.5.2 scope re-confirmation)

regimes.name: PII / Privacy (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, state laws)
regimes.applies_when: personal information of EU residents (GDPR) or of residents of California and ~20 other US states is collected or processed
regimes.challenge: unanswered -- select applicable or not (`wall compliance privacy ...`)

controls.statement: Lawful basis and notice: a named basis (GDPR) or compliant notice + opt-out (CCPA/CPRA) per processing purpose
Minimization and purpose limitation: collect what the purpose needs, nothing more
Subject rights served: access, deletion, correction, portability, opt-out of sale/share
Security of processing (GDPR art. 32): appropriate technical and organizational measures
Cross-border transfers: residency and transfer mechanisms per jurisdiction
Breach clocks: 72-hour authority notice (GDPR) and state-law equivalents
Processor contracts: DPAs with every processor -- a hosted LLM included
Automated decision-making: risk assessments and opt-outs (CPRA 2026 regulations)

regimes.name: Government reach (FedRAMP, CJIS, CLOUD Act, export)
regimes.applies_when: US federal agencies are customers (FedRAMP), criminal justice information is touched (CJIS), or data faces law-enforcement reach / export control
regimes.challenge: unanswered -- select applicable or not (`wall compliance government ...`)

controls.statement: FedRAMP: authorization path chosen (Rev5 baseline or 20x), boundary defined, continuous monitoring
CJIS Security Policy (v6.x, NIST 800-53 aligned): CJI identified and controls mapped
Residency and reach: provider and region choices evaluated against CLOUD Act / Patriot Act exposure
Export control: ITAR/EAR-controlled technical data identified and segregated

regimes.name: Sector rules (SOX, GLBA, FERPA)
regimes.applies_when: public-company financial reporting (SOX), consumer financial data (GLBA), or education records (FERPA) are in scope
regimes.challenge: unanswered -- select applicable or not (`wall compliance sector ...`)

controls.statement: SOX ICFR: change control and access evidence over systems feeding financial reports
GLBA Safeguards Rule: written infosec program, risk assessment, MFA, encryption, vendor oversight
FERPA: education records identified, disclosures consent-gated, directory-info opt-outs honored

regimes.name: NIST (CSF 2.0, SP 800-171 r3, SSDF 800-218)
regimes.applies_when: a contract, customer or program requires NIST alignment: CSF 2.0 as the named framework, 800-171 for CUI in a federal supply chain, SSDF attestation for software sold to the US government
regimes.challenge: unanswered -- select applicable or not (`wall compliance nist ...`)

controls.statement: CSF Govern: risk strategy, roles, policy, oversight and supply-chain risk management established and owned
CSF Identify: assets, risks and improvement opportunities inventoried and assessed
CSF Protect: identity and access, awareness, data security, platform security, resilience
CSF Detect: continuous monitoring and adverse-event analysis in place
CSF Respond: incident management, analysis, reporting and mitigation exercised
CSF Recover: recovery execution and communications planned and tested
SP 800-171 r3 (conditional): CUI identified, controls mapped, the self-assessment score current and true
SSDF SP 800-218: secure-development practices mapped for the software produced; attestation ready where a buyer requires it

regimes.name: FDA-regulated software (SaMD/SiMD, QMSR, 524B, Part 11)
regimes.applies_when: the software is a medical device (SaMD), is embedded in or controls one (SiMD), or produces records supporting an FDA-approved application (drug, biologic, device)
regimes.challenge: unanswered -- select applicable or not (`wall compliance fda ...`)

controls.statement: QMSR quality system with design controls established (ISO 13485-aligned, in force 2026-02)
IEC 62304 lifecycle + IEC 81001-5-1 security activities: safety class assigned; secure development and maintenance planned to them
Premarket pathway identified (510(k) / De Novo / PMA) with software documentation at the level the guidance sets
524B cyber-device duties per the 2025 final guidance: SBOM, secure development framework, vulnerabilities monitored and disclosed, updates deliverable
Part 11: electronic records and signatures trustworthy wherever records support a regulated submission
Postmarket: complaint handling, Part 803 adverse-event reporting, corrections and removals ready
Change control: whether a modification needs a new submission is decided in writing; AI-enabled change rides a PCCP (Dec 2024 final, all AI functions)
